improvements: Dedicated operations gain owner-gated operator consoles, native Aspire telemetry shortcuts, and more explicit Workspace and organization controls.
Signed Executor update feeds and release-asset checks support in-place upgrades without replacing an enrolled Workspace identity.
Session tools gain safer attachment transfers, bounded Git context inspection, and clearer controls for scheduled tasks and long-running processes.
fixes: High-risk shell authorization keeps Executor dispatch bound to the Session Workspace and reports the actual denial reason without weakening exact-call checks.
Native Session compaction shows progress promptly, and empty Sessions admit model changes and compaction without an unrelated filesystem text-admission error.
Workspace attachment saves fail promptly when the Executor lacks transfer support; existing Executor services are detected before a new invitation is consumed.
knownIssues: Owner-authenticated Session operations still require an authenticated production acceptance run; local tests alone do not establish that acceptance.
Release assets must pass exact-tag qualification and signature checks before publication.

fixes: Empty native Copilot Sessions admit model changes and compaction before POSIX mount and event projection, avoiding a spurious text-admission denial.
knownIssues: This local Dedicated update does not itself constitute an authenticated Owner UI acceptance run.

improvements: Dedicated Platform adds fenced Runtime ownership, durable Session and Executor recovery, independent Dashboard updates, and Owner-controlled administration.
The Dashboard restores Workspace installation, Session navigation, connection health, notifications, and desktop controls with clearer account and timing views.
Private Cloud adds authenticated tenant isolation, persistent authority and export paths, and durable background work.
fixes: Dedicated Executor invitation serves the public installer through the Runtime ingress instead of returning 404.
The Dashboard connection status dialog remains inside the viewport when opened from the header.
Release and acceptance checks bind Windows Executor and ConPTY assets, Portable OCI images, and signed Private Cloud bundles to the exact candidate revision.
knownIssues: Dedicated and Private Cloud lifecycle certification remains preview-only; public distribution of signed artifacts is not production support.
Private Cloud NFS remains experimental and requires independent full-stack acceptance; use local-volume storage by default.
Linux arm64 native Portable assets remain outside the required acceptance matrix.

improvements: Dashboard workspace and Session explorers use clearer hierarchy, spacing, weights, and status treatments while retaining compact information density.
fixes: Dashboard explorer rows now reserve touch action space and scale phone row heights with their typography, preventing labels and controls from clipping.
Private Cloud candidate gating now requires fresh-install acceptance from the exact signed draft bundle with the native JavaScript Operator before promotion evidence can be accepted.
knownIssues: This is a beta: Windows x64 Portable Host and Executor dual-deployment work is still being validated and is not certified by this release note.
A previous Portable OCI isolated-VM attempt failed during the Socket.IO handshake with HTTP 403; exact-tag isolated-VM acceptance must be rerun successfully before candidate promotion.
Private Cloud and Portable OCI still require exact-tag acceptance evidence, immutable image digests, and the remaining release gates before public promotion.

improvements: Private Cloud installs from its signed Compose bundle with a Node.js 22+ JavaScript Operator, bundled identity option, and single-host local-volume storage by default.

Windows x64 Portable Host uses the Node.js 22+ CJS asset with matching Copilot runtime files; Windows x64 Executor ships as a separate native binary with the ConPTY companion and PowerShell installer.
Linux x64 Portable container distribution packages one Host and embedded Dashboard, independent of the three-service Private Cloud deployment.
Linux x64 and macOS x64/arm64 Executors remain native by default; self-contained native Host and Dedicated binaries are manual qualification artifacts only.
fixes: Private Cloud fresh-install acceptance now proves the candidate from the exact signed draft bundle rather than using the previous release as initial-install evidence.

Windows installation sessions require the exact Executor, ConPTY, and installer assets with matching release checksums; the Windows workspace build now selects real packages rather than silently building none.

The bundled Private Cloud Operator waits for its identity proxy and application healthchecks without falsely requiring a Zitadel binary healthcheck; fresh acceptance starts its authenticated model fixture only after the real installation owns the egress network.
Portable OCI verifies GitHub's real OCI SLSA provenance with the GitHub attestation verifier, and independently verifies its Cosign-signed SPDX SBOM after installing candidate dependencies.

Private Cloud restart acceptance verifies an external Runtime's persisted Session projection, hydrated queue and completed authenticated model reply rather than assuming Kernel-only replay history exists.
knownIssues: This is a beta: a draft release is not certification; Private Cloud and Portable OCI require exact-tag isolated-VM evidence before public promotion.
NFS remains an explicit experimental Private Cloud option and has no full-stack acceptance evidence; use local-volume by default.
Linux arm64 Executor is not in the default matrix. Windows Portable Host needs Node.js 22+ and adjacent Copilot runtime files; Host CJS alone cannot serve a Windows Executor installer.
GHCR Portable and Private Cloud package visibility must be reviewed before public promotion; image tags are not substitutes for signed immutable digests.
The beta temporarily accepts only Grype CVE-2026-95619 in gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1 and libstdc++6 version 14.2.0-19 until 2026-10-14; the Debian advisory has no fix and the residual risk remains.

improvements: The production Dashboard now presents denser Session context, usage, storage, workspace, sub-agent, and message metadata without reducing text readability.
Ask User Choice supports compact single-choice, multiple-choice, and custom-response workflows across the Dashboard, shared protocol, and Host runtime.
A production-component browser prototype harness now exercises representative Dashboard states without connecting to real Session data.
fixes: Pending Ask User Choice requests remain visible when Copilot reports an intermediate idle state before the user responds.
Sidebar, pinned-message, progress, timing, hidden-item, and responsive tab layouts now preserve their intended geometry across supported viewport sizes.
knownIssues: Dedicated and Private Cloud lifecycle certification remains preview-only as described in the release support policy.
Windows and Linux arm64 native Portable assets remain outside the supported v0.2.0 release matrix.

improvements: Private Cloud images now contain only the Node.js runtime libraries and package inventory required by the shipped services.
The reduced runtime remains non-root and preserves CA certificates, time-zone data, DNS resolution, and writable temporary storage.
fixes: Private Cloud release scans no longer fail on an unused OpenSSL package inherited from the upstream distroless image.
knownIssues: Dedicated and Private Cloud lifecycle certification remains preview-only as described in the release support policy.

improvements: Adjacent Thinking updates now appear as one compact visual group with navigation in the header.
Per-turn timing expands inline, and failed turns without an assistant reply retain their timing details.
Session storage review now provides safer cleanup planning, corruption isolation, and clearer retained-data accounting.
The workspace browser, sidebar Session cards, full-screen terminal behavior, and responsive Dashboard layouts are more consistent.
fixes: Copilot CLI discovery and queued message delivery remain available across local redeployments.
Cleanup plans no longer invalidate themselves while inspecting interrupted external-runtime Sessions.
Socket.IO now uses a patched Engine.IO dependency chain.
Dedicated Ingress shutdown waits for active admission reconciliation before releasing its storage.
knownIssues: Dedicated and Private Cloud lifecycle certification remains preview-only as described in the release support policy.

improvements: Running Sessions in the left sidebar now use the same ambient text treatment as Thinking activity.
The Desktop connection screen now separates first-time setup from endpoint changes.
Manual Desktop update checks now report when the installed version is current.
fixes: Conversation history hidden with `/clear` now stays hidden for that Session after refresh, reconnect, or service restart.
The right sidebar now defaults to Files and restores the last selected tab independently for each Session.
Linux Desktop microphone requests now use an explicit, origin-scoped native permission flow.
Copilot CLI discovery now remains available after a local redeployment.
knownIssues: Desktop microphone permission has been validated by automated native tests; installation still requires the normal operating-system permission prompt.
